Purpose and Decision

Audience, decision target, and evidence ladder

Audience: readers new to the project deciding which sampling method to use under explicit budget caps.

Decision: choose the method/cap that best balances aggregate accuracy, representational coverage, and operational cost on the fixed 2,800-session synthetic population.

Aggregate accuracy

Absolute aggregate MAE (lower is better).

Representational coverage

Concept coverage, use-case coverage (classification-derived/provisional), and agent coverage (higher is better).

Operational cost

Actual/Nominal token ratio relative to a 15k planning conversion.

Definitions

  • Cap = per-run selected session count target.
  • MAE = absolute difference between estimated and census pass rates.
  • Concept coverage = represented concept share in the selected sample.
  • Use-case coverage = represented Maven use-case share (classification-derived/provisional).
  • Agent coverage = represented agent share in selected sessions.

How to read this report

  1. Use Executive Recommendations to shortlist method/cap options.
  2. Check data provenance and Maven ambiguity caveats.
  3. Read question-oriented comparative results and takeaways.
  4. Use the Interactive Explorer and sentinel drilldown for deeper checks.

Dataset and Ground Truth

Two corpora, normalization, and bounded evidence examples

dense_2500: 2,500 sessions, 5 named agents (500 each), seed 3652026, scenario/difficulty/variety/behavior flags with templated tool calls and pass/fail narration; outputs/manifests retained while generator source is absent from this workspace.

historical_300: 300 sessions, 100 agents from BPS converted by synthetic_data/a365_historical_300/build_a365_otel.py; pass/fail copied from upstream expected field with deterministic IDs/timestamps where needed; original BPS authoring is outside this workspace.

Combined census: 2800 sessions, 105 agents, pass rate 71.1786%. Source pass rates: dense_2500 72.2000% and historical_300 62.6667%.

OTLP-style traces are normalized into EvaluationUnit rows (unit IDs, turns, tools); expected labels are joined only after sample membership is frozen. Source-synthetic fields are distinct from report-derived snippets.

Maven Business Use-Case Assignment

Workflow diagnostics, thresholds, and provisional coverage caveat

Workflow: cleaning, per-turn request/response embeddings with text-embedding-3-small, real v6 request/response centroids, top-5 agreement/corroboration/late-fusion, 0.30 low-confidence sentinel, 0.70 session early-stop, otherwise maximum similarity assignment.

This section describes classification behavior diagnostics, not an accuracy benchmark or external validation of the assigned use cases.

Observed bundle: Ambiguous 2569 (91.8%), Corroborated 146, Agree 85; confidence level 1=2564; Below-0.30 fallback=23; max similarity 0.690. Use-case coverage is therefore provisional.

Per-corpus diagnostics: dense_2500 n=2500, mean sim 0.527, status [('Ambiguous', 2486), ('Corroborated', 14)]. historical_300 n=300, mean sim 0.499, status [('Corroborated', 132), ('Agree', 85), ('Ambiguous', 83)], confidence [('2', 118), ('3', 81), ('1', 78), ('undetermined', 23)].

Takeaway: Status mix is dominated by Ambiguous, so use-case coverage remains classification-derived/provisional.

What this shows: Similarity values cluster below the 0.70 early-stop threshold; 0.30 and 0.70 are operational cutoff annotations for weak fallback and strong assignment.

Experiment Design and Metrics

Fixed population design, replay pairing, and metric intent

Design: fixed population, caps 64/128/256/512/1024, 30 paired deterministic seeds, and membership frozen before expected-label joins. Estimand is pass-rate estimation quality and representation behavior on this fixed population.

Descriptive spread is reported as mean/median/p05/p95; these are not inferential confidence intervals.

15k is a planning-only conversion from token budget to session cap; observed actual/nominal ratios (2.42% to 8.93%) are expected and do not imply selection-budget under-run.

Metric glossary

  • Absolute aggregate MAE (lower better): estimator accuracy.
  • Concept coverage (higher better): source concept representation.
  • Use-case coverage (higher better, provisional): classification-derived representation.
  • Agent coverage (higher better): cross-agent representation.
  • Actual/Nominal token ratio: operational cost context.

ARM1 global deterministic random + unweighted mean

Strong low-cap MAE baseline with simpler behavior.

ARM2 adaptive selector + same-agent IDW

Full-session embeddings and Azure Search donor retrieval with fallback chain; primary use is imputation/calibration study.

ARM3 floor then strata + unweighted mean

One-per-agent round robin to min(3, N_agent), then proportional Maven strata. The artifact-derived floor target totals 163 sessions.

ARM4 capacity-aware round robin + unweighted mean

No hard floor; emphasizes broad representation via round-robin and strata.

ARM5 ARM4-membership + Hajek ratio estimator

Coverage mirrors ARM4; only estimator differs. Can be unstable at low caps.

Token-cap conversion and equations:

Generated Methodology Narrative (Artifact-Driven)

This narrative is synthesized from artifact fields and does not depend on optional markdown richness.

Population and replay setup: caps=64, 128, 256, 512, 1024; observed trial count=30. A 30-trial spread is available in this bundle.

  1. Population and labels: full-session packet units are labeled with expected outcomes and attached metadata.
  2. Five-arm design: ARM1 global random, ARM2 embedding-IDW, ARM3 round-robin with floor, ARM4 round-robin strata balancing, ARM5 same-membership Hajek weighted estimator.
  3. Cap conversion: sample budget uses a 15k tokens/session planning conversion.
  4. Maven classifier: confidence thresholds 0.30 and 0.70 partition ambiguous vs stronger assignments.
  5. Embedding and clustering: full-session packet embeddings are grouped through Azure Search neighborhood retrieval for donor selection.
  6. IDW donor chain: observed value, exact/donor interpolation, then agent/global/prior fallback groups when donor evidence is sparse.
  7. ARM3 floor then strata: minimum floor target first (configured min-per-agent=3), then remaining budget allocated by strata.
  8. ARM4 stratification: round-robin strata exposure without hard floor completion requirement.
  9. ARM5 same-membership Hajek estimator: uses membership-aligned weighted ratio estimator for aggregate rates.
  10. Metrics and spread: MAE, concept/use-case/agent coverage, token ratio, Brier and ECE; trial spread reported as min/max descriptive ranges.
  11. Trial pairing and seeds: runs are paired by cap and seed; spread is descriptive and not inferential significance testing.
  12. Limitations: classifier ambiguity, sparse donor contexts, and cap-limited coverage can bias observed rates.

Source Methodology (Sanitized Markdown)

Sampling V6 Methodology

Scope

  • Population is the exact combined 2800-session retained synthetic corpus unless canary slicing is explicitly requested.
  • Expected labels are joined after membership freeze for every arm.

Arms

  • Arm1: global deterministic random membership.
  • Arm2: embedding-based adaptive selection replayed against the real vector index with exact-count cap and IDW estimation over the full population.
  • Arm3: agent round-robin with floor prefix.
  • Arm4: agent round-robin probability design.
  • Arm5: Hajek-weighted reuse of Arm4 membership and inclusion probabilities.

Arm2 Exact-Count Logic

  • Replays a deterministic seed order through AdaptiveSampler + AzureClusterIndex via V3EmbeddingSelector.
  • Native proposals are accepted in replay order if native_count <= cap.
  • If native_count > cap, native rows are ranked by novelty desc, rarity desc, stable hash and truncated to cap.
  • If native_count < cap, fill rows are ranked by novelty desc, rarity desc, stable hash and appended until exact cap.
  • Any fallback-signature behavior causes hard failure.
  • Azure scope is cleaned before and after each arm2 replay; settled zero remaining docs is required when the store supports scope counting.

Token Accounting

  • Nominal budget per run is cap * avg_tokens_per_session.
  • Actual token count is the sum of runtime token costs for selected unit IDs.

Maven Classification Parity

  • Each turn is mapped in order to SessionStepText(request=user_text, response=assistant_text).
  • Cleaning and token limits use classifier-native logic and cl100k_base counting.
  • Classification applies threshold early-stop then max-similarity fallback exactly as classifier implementation defines.
  • classification artifacts store no raw session text.

Estimands

  • Aggregate estimand is pass-rate over full population.
  • Arm2 uses observed+IDW imputation and reports validation diagnostics.
  • Arm5 uses Hajek ratio estimator with Arm4 inclusion probabilities.

Limitations

  • Arm2 exact-count replay introduces deterministic ranking choices when proposals exceed cap.
  • IDW is model-assisted and should be treated as an approximation, not a design-unbiased guarantee.
  • Existing dataset metadata and expected labels are synthetic and non-production.

Observation: At low caps this sentinel panel shows n=0/1 volatility and missing selections; at higher caps selected rates converge toward census rates.

Limitations and Validity

Scope and caveats for interpretation
  • Synthetic sessions and labels; this is not production-ground-truth evidence.
  • Fixed population and deterministic replays; no p-values/generalization inference.
  • Classification ambiguity is high; use-case coverage is provisional.
  • ARM2 includes model-assisted IDW assumptions and fallback behavior.
  • ARM5 weighting can be unstable at low caps.
  • 15k planning conversion is conservative and approximate.
  • Sentinel drilldown covers only five largest dense agents.

Recommendations and Next Steps

Actionable next work and update triggers

Accuracy-first: ARM1 at caps 64/128/256.

Representation-first: ARM4/ARM5, with explicit provisional use-case caveat.

Balanced objective: ARM5 at 512; ARM5 vs ARM1 at 1024 is a near-tie due to mean-median disagreement.

  1. Run a production shadow evaluation with matched cap/seed structure.
  2. Perform a labeled Maven classification audit.
  3. Calibrate nominal token conversion empirically from production traces.
  4. Increase trials only if rank ordering remains ambiguous.

Evidence that would change this decision: shadow-run rank reversal, improved classification confidence profile, or major token calibration shift.

Generated Methodology Narrative (Artifact-Driven)

This narrative is synthesized from artifact fields and does not depend on optional markdown richness.

Population and replay setup: caps=64, 128, 256, 512, 1024; observed trial count=30. A 30-trial spread is available in this bundle.

  1. Population and labels: full-session packet units are labeled with expected outcomes and attached metadata.
  2. Five-arm design: ARM1 global random, ARM2 embedding-IDW, ARM3 round-robin with floor, ARM4 round-robin strata balancing, ARM5 same-membership Hajek weighted estimator.
  3. Cap conversion: sample budget uses a 15k tokens/session planning conversion.
  4. Maven classifier: confidence thresholds 0.30 and 0.70 partition ambiguous vs stronger assignments.
  5. Embedding and clustering: full-session packet embeddings are grouped through Azure Search neighborhood retrieval for donor selection.
  6. IDW donor chain: observed value, exact/donor interpolation, then agent/global/prior fallback groups when donor evidence is sparse.
  7. ARM3 floor then strata: minimum floor target first (configured min-per-agent=3), then remaining budget allocated by strata.
  8. ARM4 stratification: round-robin strata exposure without hard floor completion requirement.
  9. ARM5 same-membership Hajek estimator: uses membership-aligned weighted ratio estimator for aggregate rates.
  10. Metrics and spread: MAE, concept/use-case/agent coverage, token ratio, Brier and ECE; trial spread reported as min/max descriptive ranges.
  11. Trial pairing and seeds: runs are paired by cap and seed; spread is descriptive and not inferential significance testing.
  12. Limitations: classifier ambiguity, sparse donor contexts, and cap-limited coverage can bias observed rates.

Core Equations

Cap from token budget: n=⌊B15000⌋

Absolute aggregate MAE: MAE=1K∑k=1K|r^k-rk|

Concept coverage: Cconcept=|Uselected∩concept||Uconcept|

IDW estimate: y^(x)=∑imwi(x)yi∑imwi(x),wi=1dp

Hajek estimator: R^H=∑inyiπi∑in1πi

Source Methodology (Sanitized Markdown)

Sampling V6 Methodology

Scope

  • Population is the exact combined 2800-session retained synthetic corpus unless canary slicing is explicitly requested.
  • Expected labels are joined after membership freeze for every arm.

Arms

  • Arm1: global deterministic random membership.
  • Arm2: embedding-based adaptive selection replayed against the real vector index with exact-count cap and IDW estimation over the full population.
  • Arm3: agent round-robin with floor prefix.
  • Arm4: agent round-robin probability design.
  • Arm5: Hajek-weighted reuse of Arm4 membership and inclusion probabilities.

Arm2 Exact-Count Logic

  • Replays a deterministic seed order through AdaptiveSampler + AzureClusterIndex via V3EmbeddingSelector.
  • Native proposals are accepted in replay order if native_count <= cap.
  • If native_count > cap, native rows are ranked by novelty desc, rarity desc, stable hash and truncated to cap.
  • If native_count < cap, fill rows are ranked by novelty desc, rarity desc, stable hash and appended until exact cap.
  • Any fallback-signature behavior causes hard failure.
  • Azure scope is cleaned before and after each arm2 replay; settled zero remaining docs is required when the store supports scope counting.

Token Accounting

  • Nominal budget per run is cap * avg_tokens_per_session.
  • Actual token count is the sum of runtime token costs for selected unit IDs.

Maven Classification Parity

  • Each turn is mapped in order to SessionStepText(request=user_text, response=assistant_text).
  • Cleaning and token limits use classifier-native logic and cl100k_base counting.
  • Classification applies threshold early-stop then max-similarity fallback exactly as classifier implementation defines.
  • classification artifacts store no raw session text.

Estimands

  • Aggregate estimand is pass-rate over full population.
  • Arm2 uses observed+IDW imputation and reports validation diagnostics.
  • Arm5 uses Hajek ratio estimator with Arm4 inclusion probabilities.

Limitations

  • Arm2 exact-count replay introduces deterministic ranking choices when proposals exceed cap.
  • IDW is model-assisted and should be treated as an approximation, not a design-unbiased guarantee.
  • Existing dataset metadata and expected labels are synthetic and non-production.

Detailed IDW, membership, taxonomy, and methodology material is printed in the corresponding sections above; it is not repeated here.
